question.text: Yellow light is used in a single slit diffraction experiment with slit width of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. If yellow light is replaced by X-rays, then the observed pattern will reveal,

options.text: that the central maximum is narrower

solution.text: For diffraction pattern to be observed, the dimension of slit should be comparable to the wave length of light. In other words, diffraction is obtained when the slit width is of the order of wavelength of light (or any electromagnetic wave) used. Here, wavelength of X-rays  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>100</mn><mtext>  </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">Å</mi><mo>)</mo><mo><</mo><mtext> </mtext><mo><</mo><mi>slit</mi><mo> </mo><mi>width</mi><mo> </mo><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. Therefore, no diffraction pattern will be observed.
